papers_read.title_as_printed: A prediction nomogram for mild cognitive impairment in type 2 diabetes mellitus based on the Chinese visceral adiposity index (Zhou, Wang, Yu & Niu, Scientific Reports 2025, 15:32393)
Mild Cognitive Impairment: Data-Driven Prediction, Risk Factors, and Workup (Fouladvand, Noshad, Goldstein, Periyakoil & Chen, Stanford; AMIA proceedings pp. 167-172)

what_each_reports.P-339: 337 hospitalised T2DM patients aged 40-75, cross-sectional, MCI = MoCA < 26 (158/337). Nomogram (age, gender, education, CVAI): AUC 0.765 (95% CI 0.705-0.826) training (apparent), 0.690 (95% CI 0.588-0.792) random validation split.
what_each_reports.P-165: Stanford Healthcare OMOP EHR, 531,387 primary-care visits of patients aged 65+ (label: at least one MCI diagnosis code within one year after the visit). 480 structured and clinical-note concepts; temporal split (train through 2019, test 2020+): random forest ROC-AUC 68.2 +/- 0.7, XGBoost 66.8 +/- 0.8, logistic regression 57.0 +/- 1.1.

quantity_a: Patient-level ROC-AUC for current MoCA-defined MCI among hospitalised T2DM adults aged 40-75 from a 4-variable nomogram (0.765 apparent training value; 0.690 validation)
quantity_b: Visit-level ROC-AUC for a recorded MCI diagnosis code appearing within one year after a primary-care visit among patients aged 65+, from 480 EHR concepts (random forest, temporal hold-out)
incompatible_if_same: No: P-339's validation AUC 0.690 (95% CI 0.588-0.792) contains P-165's 0.682; the 0.765 vs 0.682 gap compares an apparent training value with a temporal hold-out value.

gates.task: mismatch: current MCI detection by psychometric cut-off (P-339) vs prediction of a future recorded diagnosis within one year (P-165); registry codes P-339 T4 and P-165 T2, the record says T1 for both
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: single-hospital Chinese T2DM inpatients vs Stanford Healthcare EHR; the record's dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong
gates.validation_tier: mismatch for the contested figures: apparent training AUC vs temporal hold-out test
gates.modality_family: partial: both clinical/tabular, but a 4-variable anthropometric-demographic nomogram vs 480 EHR concepts including NLP-derived clinical-note terms

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both ROC-AUC, but the endpoint differs (MoCA < 26 at assessment vs an MCI diagnosis code within 12 months) and so does the unit of analysis (patients vs visits)
independence: Distinct studies, cohorts and author groups
grounds: P-339 detects current MoCA-defined MCI in diabetic inpatients, while P-165 predicts a recorded MCI diagnosis code within one year of a primary-care visit, so the endpoints and populations differ.
The unit of analysis (patients vs visits), predictor sets (4 variables vs 480 EHR concepts) and dataset family differ, with no waiver on record.
Even numerically there is no disagreement: P-339's validation AUC interval (0.588-0.792) contains P-165's 0.682.

evidence_quotes.quote: with AUC values of 0.765 (95% CI: 0.705-0.826) in the training cohort and 0.690 (95% CI 0.588-0.792) in the validation cohort (Fig. 4C, D).

Based on their Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores, participants were categorized into two groups: the normal cognition (NC) group (n = 179) and the mild cognitive impairment (MCI) group (n = 158).
Each primary care visit was assigned with a binary label indicating if the patient has at least one MCI diagnosis code within one year follow up from the time of their primary care visit.
The random forest model has a higher ROC-AUC (68.2%+/-0.7%) than xgboost and logistic regression models on the test set.

record_defects: dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong: Chinese T2DM inpatients vs Stanford EHR primary-care visits.
claim_b 'AUC 0.682 on T1': P-165 predicts a future diagnosis within one year (registry T2), not current detection.
P-165 registry Best_Metric 'not reported' although the paper reports ROC-AUC 68.2 +/- 0.7; its Sample_N_Approx '531387' counts visits, not patients (Table 1 lists 7,895 MCI and 146,991 non-MCI).
claim_a uses P-339's apparent training AUC rather than its validation AUC (0.690).
The rejection reason recorded ('Same architecture family (A1_classical)') is not a ground under the rule.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing within these two papers; the endpoint, population and unit of analysis differ in kind.
